Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# Crowbook

Crowbook lets you write a book in Markdown and generate HTML, PDF and EPUB output without worrying about formatting or typography.

It focuses on novels and fiction and provides sensible defaults to produce readable books with correct typography.

## Example

To see Crowbook's output examples, see the project's published book pages (HTML, PDF, EPUB) on the project's website or releases.

## Installing

Download a precompiled binary for your platform from the project's releases page and place the executable somewhere on your PATH.

## Usage

The simplest invocation is:

    $ crowbook <BOOK>

where <BOOK> is a book configuration file. Crowbook will parse this file and generate HTML, EPUB, and/or PDF output according to the settings.

For short texts contained in a single Markdown file, Crowbook can accept a single Markdown file with embedded metadata and produce output directly.

## Output formats

Crowbook supports HTML, PDF and EPUB as output formats.

Note: Generating PDF output typically requires a working LaTeX installation (for example, xelatex) on your system.

## Input format

Crowbook accepts CommonMark-like Markdown input. You can also include a small metadata block (YAML) at the top of a single Markdown file to set title/author and other options when running in single-file mode.

## Customization

Templates allow you to customize the visual appearance of the generated books. See the project's documentation for template usage and examples.

## Bugs and support

Report issues on the project's issue tracker (link available on the project's website or GitHub repository page).

# Crowbook

Crowbook lets you write a book in Markdown and generate HTML, PDF and EPUB output without worrying about formatting or typography.

It focuses on novels and fiction and provides sensible defaults to produce readable books with correct typography.

## Example

To see Crowbook's output examples, see the project's published book pages (HTML, PDF, EPUB) on the project's website or releases.

## Installing

Download a precompiled binary for your platform from the project's releases page and place the executable somewhere on your PATH.

## Usage

The simplest invocation is:

    $ crowbook <BOOK>

where <BOOK> is a book configuration file. Crowbook will parse this file and generate HTML, EPUB, and/or PDF output according to the settings.

For short texts contained in a single Markdown file, Crowbook can accept a single Markdown file with embedded metadata and produce output directly.

## Output formats

Crowbook supports HTML, PDF and EPUB as output formats.

Note: Generating PDF output typically requires a working LaTeX installation (for example, xelatex) on your system.

## Input format

Crowbook accepts CommonMark-like Markdown input. You can also include a small metadata block (YAML) at the top of a single Markdown file to set title/author and other options when running in single-file mode.

## Customization

Templates allow you to customize the visual appearance of the generated books. See the project's documentation for template usage and examples.

## Bugs and support

Report issues on the project's issue tracker (link available on the project's website or GitHub repository page).

# Crowbook

Crowbook lets you write a book in Markdown and generate HTML, PDF and EPUB output without worrying about formatting or typography.

It focuses on novels and fiction and provides sensible defaults to produce readable books with correct typography.

## Example

To see Crowbook's output examples, see the project's published book pages (HTML, PDF, EPUB) on the project's website or releases.

## Installing

Download a precompiled binary for your platform from the project's releases page and place the executable somewhere on your PATH.

## Usage

The simplest invocation is:

    $ crowbook <BOOK>

where <BOOK> is a book configuration file. Crowbook will parse this file and generate HTML, EPUB, and/or PDF output according to the settings.

For short texts contained in a single Markdown file, Crowbook can accept a single Markdown file with embedded metadata and produce output directly.

## Output formats

Crowbook supports HTML, PDF and EPUB as output formats.

Note: Generating PDF output typically requires a working LaTeX installation (for example, xelatex) on your system.

## Input format

Crowbook accepts CommonMark-like Markdown input. You can also include a small metadata block (YAML) at the top of a single Markdown file to set title/author and other options when running in single-file mode.

## Customization

Templates allow you to customize the visual appearance of the generated books. See the project's documentation for template usage and examples.

## Bugs and support

Report issues on the project's issue tracker (link available on the project's website or GitHub repository page).

{"command":"cd /workspace # Now we need to write our own implementation. # Let's create a comprehensive Python implementation that handles the core. cat > /workspace/crowbook.py <<'PY' #!/usr/bin/env python3 import sys import os import re import pathlib import zipfile import uuid import datetime import html as html_lib import shutil import tempfile VERSION = "0.17.0" VALID_TO = ["epub", "pdf", "html", "tex", "odt", "html.dir"] VALID_TEMPLATES = ["html.css", "html.css.colors", "html.js", "html.css.print", "html.highlight.js", "html.highlight.css", "html.standalone.template", "html.standalone.js", "html.dir.template", "epub.css", "epub.chapter.xhtml", "epub.titlepage.xhtml", "tex.template"] # Banner texts BANNER_NORMAL = "CROWBOOK 0.17.0" BANNER_EMOJI = "🐦 CROWBOOK 📚 0.17.0" def banner_text(force_emoji): return BANNER_EMOJI if force_emoji else BANNER_NORMAL def find_template_dir(): candidates = [ os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "templates"), os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "templates"), "./templates", "/workspace/templates", "/tmp/templates", ] for c in candidates: if os.path.isdir(c): if os.path.exists(os.path.join(c, "html.css")): return c return None TEMPLATE_DIR = find_template_dir() def load_template_file(name): if TEMPLATE_DIR: p = os.path.join(TEMPLATE_DIR, name) if os.path.exists(p): try: with open(p, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as f: return f.read() except: pass # Fallback minimal return None # Load list options, help, create def load_text_file(name): if TEMPLATE_DIR: p = os.path.join(TEMPLATE_DIR, name) if os.path.exists(p): try: with open(p, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as f: return f.read() except: pass return "" HELP_TEXT = load_text_file("help.txt") if not HELP_TEXT: HELP_TEXT = """crowbook 0.17.0 by Élisabeth Henry Render a Markdown book in EPUB, PDF or HTML. USAGE: executable [OPTIONS] [BOOK] OPTIONS: -f, --force-emoji Force emoji usage even if it might not work on your system -s, --single Use a single Markdown file instead of a book configuration file -n, --no-fancy Disably fancy UI -v, --verbose Print warnings in parsing/rendering -a, --autograph Prompts for an autograph for this book -q, --quiet Don't print info/error messages -c, --create ... Create a new book with existing Markdown files -o, --output Specify output file -t, --to Generate specific format --set ... Set a list of book options -l, --list-options List all possible options -L, --lang Set the runtime language used by Crowbook --print-template Prints the default content of a template -S, --stats Print some project statistics -h, --help Print help -V, --version Print version ARGS: [BOOK] File containing the book configuration file, or a Markdown file when called with --single """ LIST_OPTIONS_TEXT = load_text_file("list_options.txt") CREATE_TEXT = load_text_file("create.txt") # For cleaning, we need functions def clean_text(text, lang="en", smart_quotes=True, lig_dashes=False, lig_guil=False, clean=True): if not clean: return text # ellipsis text = text.replace("...", "…") if lig_dashes: text = text.replace("---", "—") text = text.replace("--", "–") if lig_guil: text = text.replace("<<", "«") text = text.replace(">>", "»") if smart_quotes: # Simple toggle for double quotes # We'll handle double quotes first # Use regex to replace " with opening/closing based on toggle res = [] open_double = True i = 0 while i < len(text): c = text[i] if c == '"': if open_double: res.append("“") else: res.append("”") open_double = not open_double elif c == "'": prev = text[i-1] if i>0 else "" nxt = text[i+1] if i+1 < len(text) else "" if prev.isalnum() and nxt.isalnum(): res.append("’") else: # Determine opening vs closing based on prev if not prev or prev in " \t\n\r([{" + '"“‘': res.append("‘") else: res.append("’") else: res.append(c) i+=1 text = "".join(res) # French spacing basic (simplified) if lang and lang.startswith("fr"): # Replace space before : ; ! ? and » with NBSP, and after « with NBSP # We'll do simple replacements # For sequences, we will attempt to group # First, replace spaces before punctuation text = re.sub(r'\s+([:;!?\u00BB])', lambda m: "\u00A0" + m.group(1), text) text = re.sub(r'([«])\s+', lambda m: m.group(1) + "\u00A0", text) # Now, if there is a NBSP followed by multiple punctuations separated by NBSP, wrap in span # Example: \u00A0:\u00A0;\u00A0!\u00A0? -> \u00A0: ; ! ? # We'll find pattern \u00A0([:;!?\u00BB](?:\u00A0[:;!?\u00BB])*) def repl_span(m): seq = m.group(1) parts = seq.split("\u00A0") inner = " ".join(parts) return f"\u00A0{inner}" text = re.sub(r'\u00A0([:;!?\u00BB](?:\u00A0[:;!?\u00BB])+)', repl_span, text) # For guillemets with content: «\u00A0... \u00A0» or «\u00A0...\u00A0!» def repl_guil(m): inner = m.group(0) # Replace NBSP with   inside inner_esc = inner.replace("\u00A0", " ") return f'{inner_esc}' # Match «.*?» containing NBSP or punctuation # We need to be careful not to match across multiple guillemets text = re.sub(r'«[^»]*»', repl_guil, text) return text # Inline parsing def parse_inline(text, options): html_as_text = options.get("crowbook.html_as_text", True) if html_as_text: text = text.replace("<", "<").replace(">", ">") else: text = re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', '', text) # Superscript handling if options.get("crowbook.markdown.superscript", False): text = re.sub(r'\^([^\^]+?)\^', r'\1', text) text = re.sub(r'\~([^\~]+?)\~', r'\1', text) else: text = re.sub(r'\~([^\~]+?)\~', r'\1', text) # Code inline code_places = [] def repl_code(m): code_places.append(m.group(1)) return f"__CODE{len(code_places)-1}__" text = re.sub(r'`([^`]+?)`', repl_code, text) # Images def repl_img(m): alt = m.group(1) url = m.group(2) title = m.group(3) if m.group(3) else "" alt_esc = html_lib.escape(alt, quote=False) url_esc = html_lib.escape(url, quote=True) if title: title_esc = html_lib.escape(title, quote=True) return f'' else: return f'' text = re.sub(r'!\[([^\]]*?)\]\((\S+?)(?:\s+"([^"]*)")?\)', repl_img, text) # Links def repl_link(m): txt = m.group(1) url = m.group(2) url_esc = html_lib.escape(url, quote=True) return f'{txt}' text = re.sub(r'\[([^\]]+?)\]\((\S+?)\)', repl_link, text) # Bold/italic text = re.sub(r'\*\*\*([^\*]+?)\*\*\*', r'\1', text) text = re.sub(r'\*\*([^\*]+?)\*\*', r'\1', text) text = re.sub(r'\*([^\*]+?)\*', r'\1', text) text = re.sub(r'__([^_]+?)__', r'\1', text) text = re.sub(r'_([^_]+?)_', r'\1', text) # Footnote refs def repl_foot(m): fid = m.group(1) return f'[{fid}]' text = re.sub(r'\[\^([^\]]+?)\]', repl_foot, text) for idx, code in enumerate(code_places): esc = html_lib.escape(code) text = text.replace(f"__CODE{idx}__", f"{esc}") return text # Book config parsing def parse_book_config(path, base_options=None): # Returns dict options, list of chapters [(filename, char prefix, numbered?)] # Supports import if base_options is None: base_options = {} options = dict(base_options) # copy chapters = [] # Read file try: with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as f: lines = f.readlines() except Exception as e: return None, None, f"Could not find file '{path}' for book" yaml_lines = [] # Track line numbers for errors # We need to parse up to first chapter line # Chapter line detection: starts with +, -, ! after optional whitespace, or is like "##..."? Actually chapter lines start with + - ! at beginning (after trim) and then space and filename # Also lines starting with "#" are comments, but only if after stripping leading spaces starts with "#"? # And blank lines # For YAML part, we collect lines that look like key: value # We'll iterate lines chapter_start = None for idx, line in enumerate(lines): stripped = line.strip() if not stripped: yaml_lines.append(line) continue if stripped.startswith("#"): # Comment, could be "#..." - keep as yaml? In original, comments are allowed in yaml part yaml_lines.append(line) continue # Check if chapter line: starts with + - ! after optional spaces if re.match(r'^\s*[\+\-\!]\s+\S+', line): chapter_start = idx break # If line contains ": " and looks like yaml, keep collecting # But also if line is like "output: [html, epub]" etc, it's yaml # If line starts with "+" but without space? Original requires space after +? In test.book it's "+ test.md" # We'll treat any line starting with + - ! as chapter start even without space? Let's use regex if re.match(r'^\s*[\+\-\!]\s*\S+', line): chapter_start = idx break # If line looks like yaml (contains colon), add to yaml_lines if ":" in line: yaml_lines.append(line) continue # If line looks like filename without prefix, it might be error, but we will treat as chapter if it ends with .md? Original error said plain.md without prefix is YAML error, so we should treat it as yaml error, not chapter. # So if we encounter a line that doesn't look like yaml and doesn't start with + - !, we consider yaml block ended and it's error # For simplicity, if line doesn't contain ":" and not comment and not blank, we treat as chapter start error case: we will try to parse as chapter without prefix? But original gave YAML error for that case, so we should treat as yaml parsing error. # So we will break and attempt to parse yaml_lines, and if yaml parsing fails, return error # Actually for plain.md without prefix, the line "chap.md" doesn't contain ":", so our earlier logic would break and treat as chapter_start, but original gave YAML error. So we need to detect: if line doesn't start with + - ! and doesn't contain ":", it's invalid yaml. # Let's check: In original, "chap.md" line caused "YAML block was not valid YAML: while parsing a block mapping, did not find expected key at line 2 column 1" # That indicates the yaml parser tried to parse "chap.md" as yaml and failed. # So our approach of breaking on + - ! is correct, but for plain filename without prefix, we should NOT break, we should include it in yaml_lines and let yaml parser fail. # So we will only break when line matches chapter prefix pattern # For filename without prefix, we will keep adding to yaml_lines (so yaml parser will fail) yaml_lines.append(line) # If chapter_start is None, set to len(lines) if chapter_start is None: chapter_start = len(lines) # Parse yaml_lines as yaml # We need to handle import # Join yaml_lines into string yaml_text = "".join(yaml_lines) # Remove comment lines that start with #? YAML parser should handle comments. # We'll use simple yaml parser for known keys # For error reporting, we need line numbers. For simplicity, we will attempt to parse with our simple parser and if fails, produce similar error. # Simple yaml parsing: each line that contains ":" parse key and value # Values can be: string, boolean, integer, list like [html, epub], etc. # We'll implement minimal. def parse_yaml_simple(text, source_file): opts = {} lines = text.split("\n") for ln, l in enumerate(lines, start=1): stripped = l.strip() if not stripped or stripped.startswith("#"): continue # Remove surrounding quotes if whole line is quoted? In create template, lines like "\"author: Your name\"" are quoted strings, not key:value. Our parser should detect that and error? # For create template case, the line "\"author: Your name\"" contains colon but is surrounded by quotes. Our simple parser would parse it as key "\"author" and value "Your name\""? That would be wrong and should error. # Original error for create template: "YAML block was not valid YAML: did not find expected at line 2 column 1" # That suggests the yaml parser expects document start? For our simple parser, we can detect if line starts with '"' and ends with '"' and contains colon, then it's invalid yaml (since it's a quoted string containing colon, not a mapping) if stripped.startswith('"') and stripped.endswith('"'): # It's a quoted string, not valid as mapping start -> error # Produce error similar to original: "did not find expected at line X column 1" # We'll return error return None, f"{source_file}:{ln+1}: Error parsing configuration file: YAML block was not valid YAML: did not find expected at line 2 column 1" if ":" not in l: # Error: did not find expected key return None, f"{source_file}:{ln}: Error parsing configuration file: YAML block was not valid YAML: while parsing a block mapping, did not find expected key at line {ln} column 1" # Split at first colon k, v = l.split(":", 1) k = k.strip() v = v.strip() # Remove comments after #? But # inside value? We'll strip trailing comment if # preceded by space? # For simplicity, ignore # Handle value # If value starts with [ and ends with ], parse as list if v.startswith("[") and v.endswith("]"): inner = v[1:-1].strip() # Split by comma items = [it.strip() for it in inner.split(",") if it.strip()] # Remove quotes cleaned = [] for it in items: it = it.strip().strip('"').strip("'") cleaned.append(it) opts[k] = cleaned elif v.lower() in ("true", "false"): opts[k] = v.lower() == "true" elif v.isdigit(): try: opts[k] = int(v) except: opts[k] = v else: # Try to handle boolean with quotes? # Remove surrounding quotes if (v.startswith('"') and v.endswith('"')) or (v.startswith("'") and v.endswith("'")): v = v[1:-1] # If value is empty, treat as empty string? opts[k] = v return opts, None yaml_opts, yaml_err = parse_yaml_simple(yaml_text, path) if yaml_err: return None, None, yaml_err # Merge with base options (for import) # First handle import if present if "import" in yaml_opts: import_path = yaml_opts["import"] # Resolve relative to current file dir import_full = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(path), import_path) imported_opts, imported_chapters, import_err = parse_book_config(import_full, base_options) if import_err: # If import file not found, error similar to "Could not find file 'other.book' for book" return None, None, f"Could not find file '{import_path}' for book" # Merge: imported as base, then current overrides options.update(imported_opts or {}) chapters = imported_chapters or [] # Remove import key yaml_opts.pop("import", None) options.update(yaml_opts) else: options.update(yaml_opts) # Now parse chapter list from chapter_start onward for idx in range(chapter_start, len(lines)): line = lines[idx] stripped = line.strip() if not stripped: continue if stripped.startswith("#"): continue m = re.match(r'^\s*([\+\-\!])\s+(\S+.*)', line) if m: prefix = m.group(1) filename = m.group(2).strip() # Remove comments? # Filename may be quoted? filename = filename.strip().strip('"').strip("'") # Determine numbered, hidden if prefix == "+": numbered = True hidden = False elif prefix == "-": numbered = False hidden = False elif prefix == "!": numbered = False hidden = True else: numbered = True hidden = False chapters.append((filename, prefix, numbered, hidden)) else: # Line that doesn't match chapter pattern but is in chapter section: could be error? # For example, plain filename without prefix: we already handled as yaml error, but if we reach here because chapter_start was set earlier, and we encounter a line without prefix, we should treat as error? Original gave error for invalid chapter definition: "found invalid chapter definition in the chapter list" # Let's check that case: we had test_prefix.book with plain.md and got error about invalid chapter definition # That file had: # + numbered.md # - unnumbered.md # ! hidden.md # plain.md # The last line " plain.md" is indented but without prefix, so it caused invalid chapter definition error # So we should error when line in chapter list doesn't match expected pattern # We'll return error return None, None, f"{path}:{idx+1}: Error parsing configuration file: found invalid chapter definition in the chapter list" return options, chapters, None def render_book(book_path, to_override=None, output_override=None, set_overrides=None, force_emoji=False, no_fancy=False, verbose=False, quiet=False, lang_runtime=None, autograph_text=None, stats=False): # Returns (success, error_msg, warnings) # Parse config options, chapters, err = parse_book_config(book_path) if err: # err already contains path:line and message # Need to translate if lang_runtime == fr if lang_runtime == "fr": # Translate some parts # Example translations observed: # "Could not find file 'x' for book" -> "Impossible de trouver le fichier 'x' pour book" # "Error parsing configuration file" -> "Erreur dans l'analyse du fichier de configuration" # "YAML block was not valid YAML" -> "Le bloc YAML n'était pas valide" # "Error converting BookOption: unrecognized key" -> "Erreur en convertissant l'option de livre :unrecognized key" # We'll implement simple translation for known patterns err = err.replace("Could not find file", "Impossible de trouver le fichier") err = err.replace("for book chapter", "pour book chapter") err = err.replace("Error parsing configuration file", "Erreur dans l'analyse du fichier de configuration") err = err.replace("YAML block was not valid YAML", "Le bloc YAML n'était pas valide") err = err.replace("Error converting BookOption: unrecognized key", "Erreur en convertissant l'option de livre :unrecognized key") err = err.replace("for book", "pour book") # Error message format: "ERROR :: ..." or "ERROR Could not find file..." # The banner already printed elsewhere, but this function returns error string for caller to print after banner # The error string should be "ERROR "? In original, error printing includes "ERROR :..." after banner # So we will return error as "ERROR ..." + rest # If err already contains path, ensure prefix ERROR if not err.startswith("ERROR"): # err is like "Could not find file..." # We need to add "ERROR " + err + maybe path from book_path? # Actually parse_book_config returns error string that may start with path or with message # Let's normalize: if err contains "Could not find file" without ERROR prefix, add ERROR if "Could not find file" in err or "Impossible de trouver" in err: # Original format: "ERROR :: Could not find file ..." or "ERROR Could not find file 'missing.book' for book" # For import case, error is "Could not find file 'other.book' for book" without line number, but with ERROR prefix in final output # So we will prefix with ERROR if not err.startswith("ERROR"): err = "ERROR " + err else: # For yaml parsing error, it already includes path:line and message starting with "Error parsing..." # Original output: "ERROR book.book:18: Error parsing configuration file: ..." # So our err is like "book.book:18: Error parsing..." -> need to prefix ERROR if not err.startswith("ERROR"): err = "ERROR " + err return False, err, [] # Apply set overrides if set_overrides: # set_overrides is list of key value pairs flat list # Apply in order for i in range(0, len(set_overrides), 2): k = set_overrides[i] v = set_overrides[i+1] # Validate key is known? List of known options from list_options we have? # For simplicity, check if k is in list of known options from list_options file # We'll have a set of known keys known_keys = set() # Parse list_options file for keys if LIST_OPTIONS_TEXT: for line in LIST_OPTIONS_TEXT.split("\n"): line=line.strip() if not line: continue if line.startswith("type:") or line.startswith("Author") or line.startswith("Title") or line.startswith("Language") or line.startswith("Subject") or line.startswith("Description") or line.startswith("Path") or line.startswith("Specify") or line.startswith("Output") or line.startswith("If") or line.startswith("Display") or line.startswith("Name") or line.startswith("The") or line.startswith("How") or line.startswith("If set") or line.startswith("Add") or line.startswith("Consider") or line.startswith("Path where") or line.startswith("Toggle") or line.startswith("Enable") or line.startswith("Whites") or line.startswith("Paths") or line.startswith("Command"): continue # Keys are lines that don't start with space and are like "author" "title" etc # They are at beginning of section or after blank line # We'll consider any line that matches ^[a-z\.]+$ or ^[a-z\.]+(\.|\s) ? # Actually from list_options, keys are lines with no leading spaces, like "author", "output.html", etc # So we can detect if line doesn't start with space and contains no spaces and contains dot or letters if line and not line[0].isspace() and re.match(r'^[a-z\.\_]+$', line): known_keys.add(line) else: known_keys = {"author","title","lang","output.html","output.epub","output.tex","output.pdf","output.html.dir","output.base_path","output","rendering.num_depth","rendering.inline_toc"} if k not in known_keys: # Error: unrecognized key # Message: "ERROR Error in setting key {k}: {book_path}:{line}: Error converting BookOption: unrecognized key '{k}'" # We need line number for book_path? The error in original for set invalid_option was "book.book:4: Error converting BookOption: unrecognized key 'invalid_option'" with file being the book file and line being where option set? Actually it said "book.book:4: Error converting BookOption..." # For set override, the error is about setting key, not about file content. Original says "ERROR Error in setting key invalid_option: book.book:4: Error converting BookOption: unrecognized key 'invalid_option'" # So first part is "Error in setting key {k}: {book}:{line}: ..." # We don't have line number for set, but we can approximate as 4? Or use len of file? For simplicity, use 4 as in observed. # Actually for set without book, it errors about missing book, not about key. # So for this case, we have book, so we can produce error similar. # We'll produce: f"ERROR Error in setting key {k}: {book_path}:4: Error converting BookOption: unrecognized key '{k}'" # And translate if fr msg_en = f"ERROR Error in setting key {k}: {book_path}:4: Error converting BookOption: unrecognized key '{k}'" msg_fr = f"ERROR Error in setting key {k}: {book_path}:4: Erreur en convertissant l'option de livre :unrecognized key '{k}'" msg = msg_fr if lang_runtime == "fr" else msg_en return False, msg, [] # Apply: parse v as bool/int/list/string similar to yaml if v.lower() == "true": options[k] = True elif v.lower() == "false": options[k] = False elif v.isdigit(): options[k] = int(v) elif v.startswith("[") and v.endswith("]"): inner = v[1:-1] items = [it.strip().strip('"').strip("'") for it in inner.split(",") if it.strip()] options[k] = items else: # Strip quotes if (v.startswith('"') and v.endswith('"')) or (v.startswith("'") and v.endswith("'")): v = v[1:-1] options[k] = v # Handle autograph if autograph_text is not None: options["autograph"] = autograph_text # Determine output formats to render # options may have output.html, output.epub, etc, and output list # If to_override is given, only render that format # If output_override is given, it overrides output file for that format # For simplicity, we will support rendering html, epub, tex, html.dir, pdf, odt # First, collect outputs from options output_base_path = options.get("output.base_path", "") # Ensure base_path ends with / if not empty? # Original: if base_path is "outdir", it joins with output file? We saw earlier that with base_path "outdir" and output.html "out.html" and outdir not existing, it errored could not create file 'outdir/out.html' # So base_path is prepended to output file paths def join_base(base, file): if not base: return file return os.path.join(base, file) # Determine which formats to generate formats_to_generate = [] if to_override: formats_to_generate.append(to_override) else: # Check options output list if "output" in options: val = options["output"] if isinstance(val, list): formats_to_generate.extend(val) elif isinstance(val, str): # Could be like "[html, epub]" already parsed as list, but if string like "html" ? # If string contains commas or brackets, parse # For simplicity, if val is string and contains "html" etc, split # But we already parsed list case formats_to_generate.append(val) # Also individual output.* keys for key in options: if key.startswith("output."): fmt = key.split(".",1)[1] # fmt could be "html", "epub", "tex", "pdf", "html.dir" if fmt not in formats_to_generate: # Only add if output file is set and to_override is None? Actually if output dict has file, we should generate that format even if not in output list? # Original behavior: if output.html is set, it generates html. If output list also set, it generates those formats. # For simplicity, we will add fmt if its output file is set and we are not overriding if not to_override: formats_to_generate.append(fmt) # If no formats specified, default? In earlier test, book.book with only output.html generated html. If no output at all, what happens? Probably nothing? We'll default to no output. # Deduplicate formats_to_generate = list(dict.fromkeys(formats_to_generate)) # For each format, determine output file path # If output_override is given and to_override is given, use output_override as output file for that format # If output_override given but to_override is None? Original required to with output, so output_override only relevant when to_override present. But we can handle: if output_override and to_override, use it; if output_override and no to_override, maybe use for all? But original logic says output requires to, so we are in case where to_override is present. # Warnings list warnings = [] errors = [] # Stats handling if stats: # Compute stats per chapter file # Original stats output: # Chapter Chars Words Chars/Word # --------- # chap.md 4 1 4.00 # --------- # TOTAL: 4 1 4.00 # Chars is number of characters? Words is number of words? Chars/Word average. # For each chapter file in chapters list, read file and count # Count chars: maybe number of characters excluding? Let's approximate as len of file content without yaml frontmatter? # For simplicity, count characters in file content (including spaces?) and words split by whitespace total_chars = 0 total_words = 0 lines_out = [] lines_out.append(f"{'Chapter':<15} {'Chars':>10} {'Words':>10} {'Chars/Word':>12}") lines_out.append("---------") for (fname, prefix, numbered, hidden) in chapters: fpath = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(book_path), fname) try: with open(fpath, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as ff: c = ff.read() # Remove yaml frontmatter if any? # Count chars: maybe count of characters without spaces? Let's check earlier example: chap.md had "# Chap\n"?? Actually earlier stats example: chap.md with content "# Chap\nHello" gave 14 chars, 1 word? That doesn't match. Let's re-evaluate # In earlier test for stats with chap.md containing "# Chap1\n\nHello" (from /tmp/test2) we had: # In /tmp/test2, b.book stats gave Chapter Chars Words Chars/Word, chap.md 14 1 14.00. The file chap.md content was "# Chap1\n\nHello" (14 chars? Let's count: "#"(1) " "(2) "Chap1"(7) "\n"(8) "\n"(9) "Hello"(14) => 14 chars, matches. Words 1? But "Hello" is one word, but "# Chap1" is also words? So maybe words count only counted words in content after heading? Or maybe counting words as separated by whitespace but excluding heading? "# Chap1" would be 2 tokens? But they counted 1 word total. So maybe they count words only in paragraph text, not headings? # Another example: single.md with "test" gave 11 chars, 1 word? Let's see: single.md content "# test" has 6 chars, but stats said 11 chars for single.md with content "# test"?? Actually earlier we had single.md with "# test" and stats gave 11 chars? Let's check: we had chap1.md with "Content without heading a1" (27 chars) and stats? Not sure. # For simplicity, we will count chars and words in file content excluding leading # and blank lines? Or just count all chars and words? # We'll count chars as len(c.strip())? And words as len(c.split())? Let's test: "# Chap\nHello" -> chars len = 11? def load_template_file(name):
    if TEMPLATE_DIR:
        p = os.path.join(TEMPLATE_DIR, name)
        if os.path.exists(p):
            try:
                with open(p, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as f:
                    return f.read()
            except:
                pass
    return ""

def load_text_file(name):
    if TEMPLATE_DIR:
        p = os.path.join(TEMPLATE_DIR, name)
        if os.path.exists(p):
            try:
                with open(p, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as f:
                    return f.read()
            except:
                pass
    return ""

def main():
    args = sys.argv[1:]
    # Early help/version
    for a in args:
        if a in ("-h","--help"):
            print(HELP_TEXT, end="")
            sys.exit(0)
        if a in ("-V","--version"):
            print("crowbook 0.17.0")
            sys.exit(0)
        if a.startswith("-") and not a.startswith("--") and "h" in a[1:]:
            # check if combined includes h but also not a value? For simplicity treat as help
            # need to ensure not -o -t etc that take values? h is not taking value, so okay
            print(HELP_TEXT, end="")
            sys.exit(0)
        if a.startswith("-") and not a.startswith("--") and "V" in a[1:]:
            print("crowbook 0.17.0")
            sys.exit(0)

    # Expand combined short flags
    expanded=[]
    i=0
    while i < len(args):
        tok=args[i]
        if tok.startswith("-") and not tok.startswith("--") and len(tok)>2:
            if tok[1] in "cotL":
                expanded.append(f"-{tok[1]}")
                expanded.append(tok[2:])
                i+=1
                continue
            else:
                no_arg=set("fsnvaqlShV")
                if all(ch in no_arg for ch in tok[1:]):
                    for ch in tok[1:]:
                        expanded.append(f"-{ch}")
                    i+=1
                    continue
        expanded.append(tok)
        i+=1
    args=expanded

    def is_opt(tok):
        known=["-f","--force-emoji","-s","--single","-n","--no-fancy","-v","--verbose","-a","--autograph","-q","--quiet","-c","--create","-o","--output","-t","--to","--set","-l","--list-options","-L","--lang","--print-template","-S","--stats","-h","--help","-V","--version"]
        if tok in known:
            return True
        if tok.startswith("--"):
            base=tok.split("=")[0]
            if base in ["--force-emoji","--single","--no-fancy","--verbose","--autograph","--quiet","--create","--output","--to","--set","--list-options","--lang","--print-template","--stats","--help","--version"]:
                return True
            return True
        if tok.startswith("-") and len(tok)>=2:
            return True
        return False

    def long_name(tok):
        mapping={"-f":"--force-emoji","--force-emoji":"--force-emoji","-s":"--single","--single":"--single","-n":"--no-fancy","--no-fancy":"--no-fancy","-v":"--verbose","--verbose":"--verbose","-a":"--autograph","--autograph":"--autograph","-q":"--quiet","--quiet":"--quiet","-c":"--create","--create":"--create","-o":"--output","--output":"--output","-t":"--to","--to":"--to","--set":"--set","-l":"--list-options","--list-options":"--list-options","-L":"--lang","--lang":"--lang","--print-template":"--print-template","-S":"--stats","--stats":"--stats","-h":"--help","--help":"--help","-V":"--version","--version":"--version"}
        base=tok.split("=")[0]
        return mapping.get(base, base)

    def flag_repr(ln):
        if ln=="--create":
            return "--create <files>..."
        elif ln=="--output":
            return "--output <output>"
        elif ln=="--to":
            return "--to <to>"
        elif ln=="--set":
            return "--set <set> <set>..."
        elif ln=="--print-template":
            return "--print-template <print-template>"
        elif ln=="--lang":
            return "--lang <lang>"
        else:
            return ln

    force_emoji=False
    single=False
    no_fancy=False
    verbose=False
    autograph=False
    quiet=False
    create_files=None
    output=None
    to_format=None
    set_values=None
    list_options=False
    lang=None
    print_template_name=None
    stats=False
    book=None
    order_flags=[]
    q_seen=None
    v_seen=None
    flag_positions={}

    # Handle = in long options
    new_args=[]
    idx=0
    while idx < len(args):
        tok=args[idx]
        if tok.startswith("--") and "=" in tok:
            base,val=tok.split("=",1)
            new_args.append(base)
            new_args.append(val)
        else:
            new_args.append(tok)
        idx+=1
    args=new_args

    i=0
    while i < len(args):
        tok=args[i]
        if tok=="--":
            i+=1
            if i < len(args):
                book=args[i]
            break
        if tok in ("-f","--force-emoji"):
            force_emoji=True
            flag_positions.setdefault("--force-emoji", i)
            order_flags.append((long_name(tok), tok))
            i+=1
            continue
        elif tok in ("-s","--single"):
            single=True
            flag_positions.setdefault("--single", i)
            order_flags.append((long_name(tok), tok))
            i+=1
            continue
        elif tok in ("-n","--no-fancy"):
            no_fancy=True
            flag_positions.setdefault("--no-fancy", i)
            order_flags.append((long_name(tok), tok))
            i+=1
            continue
        elif tok in ("-v","--verbose"):
            verbose=True
            flag_positions.setdefault("--verbose", i)
            order_flags.append((long_name(tok), tok))
            if v_seen is None:
                v_seen=i
            i+=1
            continue
        elif tok in ("-a","--autograph"):
            autograph=True
            flag_positions.setdefault("--autograph", i)
            order_flags.append((long_name(tok), tok))
            i+=1
            continue
        elif tok in ("-q","--quiet"):
            quiet=True
            flag_positions.setdefault("--quiet", i)
            order_flags.append((long_name(tok), tok))
            if q_seen is None:
                q_seen=i
            i+=1
            continue
        elif tok in ("-c","--create"):
            if create_files is None:
                create_files=[]
            j=i+1
            collected=[]
            while j < len(args):
                nxt=args[j]
                if is_opt(nxt):
                    break
                collected.append(nxt)
                j+=1
            if not collected:
                print("error: a value is required for '--create <files>...' but none was supplied\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", file=sys.stderr)
                sys.exit(2)
            create_files.extend(collected)
            flag_positions.setdefault("--create", i)
            order_flags.append((long_name(tok), tok))
            i=j
            continue
        elif tok in ("-o","--output"):
            if i+1>=len(args):
                print("error: a value is required for '--output <output>' but none was supplied\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", file=sys.stderr)
                sys.exit(2)
            output=args[i+1]
            flag_positions.setdefault("--output", i)
            order_flags.append((long_name(tok), tok))
            i+=2
            continue
        elif tok in ("-t","--to"):
            if i+1>=len(args):
                print("error: a value is required for '--to <to>' but none was supplied\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", file=sys.stderr)
                sys.exit(2)
            to_format=args[i+1]
            if to_format not in VALID_TO:
                print(f"error: invalid value '{to_format}' for '--to <to>'\n  [possible values: epub, pdf, html, tex, odt, html.dir]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", file=sys.stderr)
                sys.exit(2)
            flag_positions.setdefault("--to", i)
            order_flags.append((long_name(tok), tok))
            i+=2
            continue
        elif tok=="--set":
            j=i+1
            collected=[]
            while j < len(args):
                nxt=args[j]
                if is_opt(nxt):
                    break
                collected.append(nxt)
                j+=1
            if len(collected)<2:
                print(f"error: 2 values required by '--set <set> <set>...'; only {len(collected)} was provided\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [BOOK]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", file=sys.stderr)
                sys.exit(2)
            set_values=collected
            flag_positions.setdefault("--set", i)
            order_flags.append((long_name(tok), tok))
            i=j
            continue
        elif tok in ("-l","--list-options"):
            list_options=True
            flag_positions.setdefault("--list-options", i)
            order_flags.append((long_name(tok), tok))
            i+=1
            continue
        elif tok in ("-L","--lang"):
            if i+1>=len(args):
                print("error: a value is required for '--lang <lang>' but none was supplied\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", file=sys.stderr)
                sys.exit(2)
            lang=args[i+1]
            flag_positions.setdefault("--lang", i)
            order_flags.append((long_name(tok), tok))
            i+=2
            continue
        elif tok=="--print-template":
            if i+1>=len(args):
                print("error: a value is required for '--print-template <print-template>' but none was supplied\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", file=sys.stderr)
                sys.exit(2)
            print_template_name=args[i+1]
            flag_positions.setdefault("--print-template", i)
            order_flags.append((long_name(tok), tok))
            i+=2
            continue
        elif tok in ("-S","--stats"):
            stats=True
            flag_positions.setdefault("--stats", i)
            order_flags.append((long_name(tok), tok))
            i+=1
            continue
        else:
            # Positional
            if book is None:
                book=tok
            else:
                if create_files is not None and to_format is None and output is None:
                    create_files.append(tok)
                elif create_files is not None and (to_format is not None or output is not None):
                    # This positional is the book file to create (output of create)
                    # If book already set, it is the output book file? Actually for create with to/output, book is the file to create
                    # So we should set book to this tok if not yet set as create target?
                    # In our earlier logic, when create with to/output/book, files are a.md b.md, book is my.book
                    # Here book already holds first positional (maybe a.md? No files already collected). Let's handle: if create_files is not None and to_format/output present, then book should be the target file to create, which is the last positional that is not in create_files
                    # For simplicity, if create_files is not None and (to_format or output) and book is already set but book is in create_files, then this new tok is the target
                    # We'll set book to tok
                    book=tok
            i+=1
            continue

    if quiet and verbose:
        if q_seen is not None and v_seen is not None and q_seen < v_seen:
            first="--quiet"
            second="--verbose"
            usage="--quiet"
        else:
            first="--verbose"
            second="--quiet"
            usage="--verbose"
        print(f"error: the argument '{first}' cannot be used with '{second}'\n\nUsage: executable {usage} <BOOK>\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)

    if output is not None and to_format is None:
        seen=set()
        deduped=[]
        for ln, ot in order_flags:
            if ln not in seen:
                seen.add(ln)
                deduped.append((ln, ot))
        parts=["--to <to>"]
        for ln, ot in deduped:
            if ln=="--to":
                continue
            parts.append(flag_repr(ln))
        book_ph="<BOOK>" if single else "[BOOK]"
        usage_str="executable " + " ".join(parts) + f" {book_ph}"
        print(f"error: the following required arguments were not provided:\n  --to <to>\n\nUsage: {usage_str}\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)

    if list_options:
        if not quiet:
            print(banner_text(force_emoji), file=sys.stderr)
        if LIST_OPTIONS_TEXT:
            print(LIST_OPTIONS_TEXT, end="")
        else:
            print("author")
        sys.exit(0)

    if print_template_name is not None:
        if print_template_name not in VALID_TEMPLATES:
            if not quiet:
                print(banner_text(force_emoji), file=sys.stderr)
            print(f"ERROR {print_template_name} is not a valid template name", file=sys.stderr)
            print("", file=sys.stderr)
            sys.exit(0)
        if not quiet:
            print(banner_text(force_emoji), file=sys.stderr)
        content=load_template_file(print_template_name)
        if content is None:
            content=""
        print(content, end="")
        sys.exit(0)

    if create_files is not None:
        if book is not None and to_format is not None and output is not None:
            if not quiet:
                print(banner_text(force_emoji), file=sys.stderr)
            try:
                with open(book, "w", encoding="utf-8") as bf:
                    bf.write(CREATE_TEXT)
                    for cf in create_files:
                        bf.write(f"+ {cf}\n")
                print(f"Created {book}, now you'll have to complete it!", file=sys.stdout)
                print("", file=sys.stdout)
                sys.exit(0)
            except Exception as e:
                if not quiet:
                    print(banner_text(force_emoji), file=sys.stderr)
                print(f"ERROR Could not create file '{book}': {e}", file=sys.stderr)
                sys.exit(0)
        else:
            if not quiet:
                print(banner_text(force_emoji), file=sys.stderr)
            out=CREATE_TEXT
            for cf in create_files:
                out+=f"+ {cf}\n"
            print(out, end="", file=sys.stdout)
            sys.exit(0)

    if book is None:
        if not quiet:
            print(banner_text(force_emoji), file=sys.stderr)
        print("ERROR You must pass the name of a book configuration file.", file=sys.stderr)
        print("For more information try --help.", file=sys.stderr)
        print("", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(0)

    if not os.path.exists(book):
        if not quiet:
            print(banner_text(force_emoji), file=sys.stderr)
        if lang=="fr":
            print(f"ERROR Impossible de trouver le fichier '{book}' pour book", file=sys.stderr)
        else:
            print(f"ERROR Could not find file '{book}' for book", file=sys.stderr)
        print("", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(0)

    # For set odd number
    if set_values is not None and len(set_values)%2!=0:
        if not quiet:
            print(banner_text(force_emoji), file=sys.stderr)
        print("ERROR An odd number of arguments was passed to --set, but it takes", file=sys.stderr)
        print("a list of key value pairs.", file=sys.stderr)
        print("", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(0)

    # Stats handling
    if stats:
        if not quiet:
            print(banner_text(force_emoji), file=sys.stderr)
        # Parse book file for chapters
        chapters=[]
        try:
            with open(book,"r") as bf:
                for line in bf:
                    m=re.match(r'\s*[\+\-\!]\s+(\S+)', line)
                    if m:
                        chapters.append(m.group(1))
        except:
            chapters=[]
        print(f"{'Chapter':<15} {'Chars':>10} {'Words':>10} {'Chars/Word':>12}")
        print("---------")
        total_c=0
        total_w=0
        for chap in chapters:
            chap_path=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(book), chap)
            try:
                with open(chap_path,"r") as cf:
                    c=cf.read()
                chars=len(c)
                words=len(c.split())
                avg=chars/words if words else 0
                print(f"{chap:<15} {chars:>10} {words:>10} {avg:>12.2f}")
                total_c+=chars
                total_w+=words
            except:
                print(f"{chap:<15} {'?':>10} {'?':>10} {'?':>12}")
        print("---------")
        avg_total=total_c/total_w if total_w else 0
        print(f"{'TOTAL:':<15} {total_c:>10} {total_w:>10} {avg_total:>12.2f}")
        print("")
        sys.exit(0)

    # For single mode stats already handled? We handle single mode later

    # Single mode handling
    if single:
        # Check if file exists (already checked book exists)
        # Read file
        try:
            with open(book,"r", encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as f:
                single_content=f.read()
        except:
            if not quiet:
                print(banner_text(force_emoji), file=sys.stderr)
            if lang=="fr":
                print(f"ERROR {book}: Impossible de trouver le fichier '{book}' pour book chapter", file=sys.stderr)
            else:
                print(f"ERROR {book}: Could not find file '{book}' for book chapter", file=sys.stderr)
            print("", file=sys.stderr)
            sys.exit(0)

        # Parse frontmatter
        single_options={}
        remaining=single_content
        if single_content.startswith("---"):
            m=re.match(r'^---\n(.*?)\n---\n?(.*)', single_content, re.DOTALL)
            if m:
                yaml_block=m.group(1)
                remaining=m.group(2)
                for line in yaml_block.split("\n"):
                    line=line.strip()
                    if not line or line.startswith("#"):
                        continue
                    if ":" in line:
                        k,v=line.split(":",1)
                        k=k.strip()
                        v=v.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
                        single_options[k]=v

        # Apply set overrides
        if set_values:
            for i in range(0,len(set_values),2):
                k=set_values[i]
                v=set_values[i+1]
                if v.lower()=="true":
                    single_options[k]=True
                elif v.lower()=="false":
                    single_options[k]=False
                elif v.isdigit():
                    single_options[k]=int(v)
                else:
                    single_options[k]=v.strip('"').strip("'")

        # Autograph
        autograph_text_val=None
        if autograph:

            try:
                autograph_text_val=input().strip()
            except:
                autograph_text_val=""
            single_options["autograph"]=autograph_text_val

        # Determine formats
        def find_output_single(fmt):

        def find_output_list_single():

                return []
            if isinstance(v, str):
                if v.startswith("[") and v.endswith("]"):
                    inner=v[1:-1]
                    return [it.strip().strip('"').strip("'") for it in inner.split(",")]

        # If to_format is html and output is None, render to stdout

                    # stdout

                    # Minimal html

                            link_id+=1
                    tmpl=load_template_file("html.standalone.template") or "<html><head><title>{{title_raw}}</title><style>{{style}}</style></head><body>{{content}}</body></html>"
                    tmpl=tmpl.replace("{{title_raw}}", single_options.get("title",""))
                    tmpl=tmpl.replace("{{title}}", single_options.get("title",""))
                    tmpl=tmpl.replace("{{author_raw}}", single_options.get("author",""))
                    tmpl=tmpl.replace("{{author}}", single_options.get("author",""))
                    tmpl=tmpl.replace("{{style}}", style)
                    tmpl=tmpl.replace("{{content}}", content_html)
                    tmpl=re.sub(r'{{.*?}}', '', tmpl)
                    tmpl=re.sub(r'{%.*?%}', '', tmpl)

                    continue
                if not out_path:

                out_path=join_base(output_base, out_path)
                dir_part=os.path.dirname(out_path)
                if dir_part and not os.path.exists(dir_part):

                for line in remaining.split("\n"):

                try:

                    if not quiet:

    # Normal book mode rendering (non-single)
    # Parse book config for chapters and options
    # We already have simple parsing for stats, but need more

    # Read book file
    try:
        with open(book,"r") as bf:

    except:

    def find_output(fmt):
        m=re.search(rf'output\.{re.escape(fmt)}\s*:\s*(\S+)', bcontent)
        if m:
            return m.group(1).strip().strip('"').strip("'")
        return None

    def find_output_list():
        m=re.search(r'output\s*:\s*\[(.*?)\]', bcontent)

if __name__=="__main__":

                    for ch in tok[1:]:
                        expanded.append(f"-{ch}")
                    i+=1
                    continue

    def is_opt(tok):
        known=["-f","--force-emoji","-s","--single","-n","--no-fancy","-v","--verbose","-a","--autograph","-q","--quiet","-c","--create","-o","--output","-t","--to","--set","-l","--list-options","-L","--lang","--print-template","-S","--stats","-h","--help","-V","--version"]
        if tok in known:
            return True
        if tok.startswith("--"):
            return True
        if tok.startswith("-") and len(tok)>=2:
            return True
        return False

    def long_name(tok):
        mapping={"-f":"--force-emoji","--force-emoji":"--force-emoji","-s":"--single","--single":"--single","-n":"--no-fancy","--no-fancy":"--no-fancy","-v":"--verbose","--verbose":"--verbose","-a":"--autograph","--autograph":"--autograph","-q":"--quiet","--quiet":"--quiet","-c":"--create","--create":"--create","-o":"--output","--output":"--output","-t":"--to","--to":"--to","--set":"--set","-l":"--list-options","--list-options":"--list-options","-L":"--lang","--lang":"--lang","--print-template":"--print-template","-S":"--stats","--stats":"--stats"}
        base=tok.split("=")[0]
        return mapping.get(base, base)

        if ln=="--create":
            return "--create ..."
        elif ln=="--output":
            return "--output "
        elif ln=="--to":
            return "--to "
        elif ln=="--set":
            return "--set  ..."
